bottleneck: CGRP antibodies prevent migraines for many patients, but a substantial fraction do not respond, and why is unknown. Migraine's trigger cascade — from cortical spreading depression to trigeminovascular activation to central sensitization — is described but not causally ordered, so non-responders have no rational next step and are cycled through drug classes by trial and error. The most disabling neurological disorder in young adults is still treated empirically, and the heterogeneity of migraine (with aura, without, chronic, hemiplegic) suggests multiple distinct mechanisms are being treated as one disease.
current_state: CGRP drugs are a genuine advance, yet migraine remains trial-and-error prescribing with large non-responder populations and no biomarker predicting who benefits.

title: Migraine non-responders lack mechanistic explanation
why_it_blocks: Even the newest migraine drugs fail many patients for unknown reasons, condemning them to years of guessing. Mapping the causal cascade would convert empirical prescribing into targeted therapy for a billion sufferers.
